facts.text: On this date in 1997, Princess Diana died in a Paris tunnel — triggering the largest outpouring of public grief Britain had ever recorded, with an estimated 1 million flowers left outside Kensington Palace.
On this date in 1991, Kyrgyzstan declared independence from the Soviet Union — one of five nations to do so that single week as the USSR collapsed in real time.
Indonesia spans more time zones (5) than any country in continental Europe, stretching 3,200 miles from Sumatra to Papua across an archipelago of 17,000 islands.
Monaco has more millionaires per capita than any nation on Earth — roughly one in three residents — yet maintains a public healthcare system free to all citizens.
Lagos adds an estimated 77 new residents every hour, making it the fastest-growing megacity on the planet and on track to become the world's most populous city by 2100.
On this day in 1998, Russia defaulted on its domestic debt and devalued the ruble, triggering a global panic that wiped out Long-Term Capital Management — a hedge fund run by two Nobel laureates.
On August 31, 2020, Apple and Tesla executed massive stock splits simultaneously, a coincidence so rare it had never happened on the same day between two Dow-adjacent giants before.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792 by 24 brokers — their agreement, signed on Wall Street, set a minimum commission so traders couldn't undercut each other.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit $2.46 trillion in market cap in 2022, making it worth more than the entire GDP of France — a single company outweighing a G7 nation.

The Dutch East India Company, history's first publicly traded firm, paid dividends for nearly 200 consecutive years — funded partly by monopoly spice routes that could mark up nutmeg 32,000% from source to Amsterdam.

On this date in 1897, Thomas Edison patented the Kinetoscope — but the physics of film relies on a flaw: your brain retains each frame for ~150ms, stitching still images into motion that never existed.

On August 31, 1056, Empress Theodora died, ending the Macedonian dynasty — and the bacteria on her deathbed outlived her empire by millennia. A single gram of soil holds up to a billion bacterial cells.
Your skeleton is not static. Every decade, you replace nearly all your bone mass through a process called remodeling — you are, materially, a different person than you were ten years ago.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its matter would weigh roughly 10 million tons on Earth.
The universe is not silent — it hums. The cosmic microwave background radiation is the stretched afterglow of the Big Bang, and its temperature today is precisely 2.725 Kelvin above absolute zero.

On this day in 1422, Henry V of England died at 35, having conquered most of France. He outlived his own legend so briefly that his funeral procession took longer to reach London than he'd spent as king of Paris.
On this day in 1888, Mary Ann Nichols was murdered in Whitechapel — the first confirmed Ripper victim. The killer was never identified, meaning the case remains officially open.
The fax machine was invented in 1843, before the telephone. Alexander Bain patented it while most of Europe was still lighting streets with gas lamps.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was born roughly 2,500 years after it was built, and died 2,050 years before 1969.
Oxford University began teaching students around 1096 — making it older than the Aztec Empire, older than the Black Death, and older than the existence of the word 'university' in English.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. It spread because we needed it.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home you cannot return to — or that never existed. Untranslatable, it folds nostalgia, grief, and belonging into a single breath.
On this day in 1422, Henry V of England died, leaving a nine-month-old heir. The word 'minority' entered English politics precisely to describe the crisis of a king too young to rule.
Petrichor — the smell of rain on dry earth — was nameless until 1964, when two Australian scientists coined it from Greek petra (stone) and ichor (the fluid in gods' veins).

On this day in 1997, news of Diana's death broke worldwide. The word 'paparazzi' comes from a 1960 Fellini film; Paparazzo was a mosquito-like photographer whose name Fellini chose for its irritating buzz.
On this date in 2012, Coinbase processed its first Bitcoin transaction — $13.61 worth — sent by co-founder Brian Armstrong to co-founder Fred Ehrsam. The company later peaked at a $100B valuation.

On this date in 2017, IOTA's mainnet launched, introducing a DAG-based ledger called the Tangle that required no miners and no transaction fees — a structural bet that ultimately failed to scale as promised.

Bitcoin's genesis block contains a hidden message: 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks.' Satoshi embedded a newspaper headline to timestamp the chain and editorialize in a single move.

Ethereum's EIP-1559, activated in August 2021, doesn't just smooth fees — it burns base fees permanently. Over 4 million ETH had been destroyed by 2025, making Ethereum net-deflationary during high-activity periods.

The DAO hack of 2016 drained 3.6M ETH in a single recursive call exploit. Ethereum's response — a hard fork to reverse the theft — split the chain into ETH and ETC, two live networks that still coexist today.

On this date in 2016, DeepMind published WaveNet, generating raw audio waveforms sample-by-sample at 16,000Hz — 1,600× slower than real-time. Within two years it ran faster than real-time in production at Google.

On August 31, 2012, Krizhevsky's AlexNet submission deadline passed for ImageNet. That single GPU-trained model cut the top-5 error rate by 10 percentage points, effectively ending a decade of hand-engineered vision features.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US homes, spent in a matter of months on a single model.

Transformers have no built-in notion of sequence order. Positional encodings were an afterthought added to make the architecture work at all — the original 'Attention Is All You Need' paper treats them in a single paragraph.

Chinchilla (2022) showed that most large language models up to that point were simultaneously undertrained and overparameterized — meaning researchers had spent years burning compute in exactly the wrong ratio of data to parameters.
